messages:
Anya: kicking off intake for Dedicated GA gating. Customer (regulated fintech) requires verifiable perf + cost + quality guarantees before we flip GA for private Dedicated pools.
Max: noted. can you call out the hard customer constraints we need to validate (SLA, daily tokens, model family, cost envelope)?
Anya: basics: 99.9% uptime SLA, p95 <= 150ms for 4k sequences, target cost ~ $0.30 / 1k tokens (reserved), initial models in the Llama-2 family, expected steady traffic ~2M tokens/day.
Sara: short problem stmt: customers cannot accept Dedicated as GA without an automated, auditable launch gate that combines latency, cost, and quality checks.
Sara: goals (v1):
- define measurable launch gates and acceptance tests
- automate gates via config-as-code + CI/canary pipelines
- provide rollback automation + runbooks so ops can act fast
Sara: non-goals (v1): no customer-facing gating UI, no per-route GUI knobs, no tenant-exposed SLOs.
Kai: quality gate proposal: locked eval prompt set per model family plus an agreed metric (e.g., task-specific F1 or LM NLL). Gate fails if metric degrades > 2% vs baseline.
Max: infra constraints: need routing-level canary (1%-5% traffic) to Dedicated pools, canary must run on fixed capacity (disable autoscaler), fallback to hosted-compatible variant if sustained capacity loss, perf tests must be runnable in CI with simulated customer traffic.
Anya: draft acceptance criteria (please flag holes):
1) Canary deployment created from config-as-code and routable via current traffic-split plumbing; initial split 1%-5%.
2) Perf: p95 <= 150ms measured over a 24h window using customer token-length distribution.
3) Cost: measured effective cost <= $0.35 / 1k tokens in baseline scenario (includes reserved pricing amortization).
4) Quality: automated eval harness runs hourly during canary; no regression > 2% vs baseline.
5) Safety: no PII detection failures in static log scans and sampled outputs.
6) Rollback automation: defined triggers that auto-route off and page oncall (examples: p95>200ms for 10m, error rate >1% sustained for 5m, quality regression >3%).
Max: edge cases to call out: tokenizer/build mismatches causing scoring drift; transient infra noise giving short latency spikes (need smoothing windows + sustained breach definition); quantization/precision diffs (8-bit vs fp16) that spike failures on narrow prompt classes; autoscaler cold-starts during load surges -> decide throttle vs fallback.
Kai: ownerships/questions: Research will own eval baselines for initial families and publish artifacts; who owns the canonical cost model for Dedicated? Finance or Infra?
Max: propose infra/finops pair owns initial internal cost model; external exports to customers are v2.
Sara: scope negotiation suggestion:
- v1 (MVP): config-as-code gates + CLI triggers + internal dashboards + automated canary + rollback automation + runbook.
- v2: customer-facing gating UI, per-route tolerances, exportable SLOs and tenant-visible token-level telemetry.
Sara: GA checklist (must be green before GA flip):
- pass acceptance criteria across two independent canary windows (48h each)
- runbook + rollback playbook written and practiced in drill
- SE onboarding checklist + docs
- security signoff (KMS, logging retention, private control-plane verification)
ops-bot: ci/canary-pipeline #73 status: unit tests ✅, perf harness scheduled (ETA 6h).
Max: rough plan: routing + infra work 3-4 sprints, eval harness & automation 2 sprints, docs + runbooks 1 sprint. overlap some workstreams.
Anya: next steps: assign owners, schedule 60m scoping. proposed owners: Anya (PM), Max (Eng lead), Kai (Research), Sara (Prod Ops). Meeting Thu 14:00 PT — I'll send invite.
Sara: will draft PRD skeleton and acceptance checklist after scoping, will post draft here. :thumbsup:
Max: prepping perf-run scripts, smoke queries, and a representative token-length distribution JSON to feed perf harness.
Kai: preparing eval prompt set and baseline artifacts; will post repo link when ready.
Anya: please keep short status updates here and paste CI/job links. we'll use this thread as the canonical intake note. thanks! :wave:
